items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was with Benny Carter’s band.

ctx.x: So I’m in Cab’s band. So they get the word. They ask Cab, “What do you think?” “He’s all right. He’s all right. He’s all right.” Well I was with [? (inaudible)]. I was with Benny Carter’s band. Benny Carter’s band was a triumphant band. When you worked with Benny Carter, [expletive deleted]. Everybody, they didn’t speak to you before, speak to you, because you’re with Benny Carter. Benny Carter had heard me and Johnny Williams and Walter Johnson. I don’t know why he didn’t hire, because Walter Johnson was . . .…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Then back to Lucky Millinder's band, then to Benny Carter's band.

ctx.x: band... From Baron Lee's band to Lucky Millinder's band. From Lucky Millinder's band to Jimmy Johnson's band. Then back to Lucky Millinder's band, then to Benny Carter's band. When you get into Benny Carter's band... Benny Carter organized a band like every two years. You see, he'd sit down and he'd write six arrangements. Then he'd get a new band. So he'd rehearse his arrangements, see how his arrangements are. Then he'd get two or three books of bookings, then he'd break up the band. Then he takes all his…
Yeah, you see him around right now.
